normalized.description: The space debris environment, space traffic, and the associated operational context are very dynamic. Yet, inearly spacecraft design, the expected effort for collision avoidance during the mission and disposal phasesneeds to be estimated. Existing models allow designers and operators to estimate the fuel budget.However, those are based on general assumptions and single source space surveillance data.With the introduction of the Zero Debris approach and the proliferation of space surveillance companies, theimpact of collision avoidance operations goes beyond fuel estimation and now requires to account for, amongothers, mission time loss, requiredground support, and varying data providers.This activity aims to create a software model building on current knowledge in mission operations in the contextof collision avoidance to facilitate state-of-the-art estimates for collision avoidance efforts. Based on more than20 years of collision avoidance practices, a robust assessment framework could be created, to be used:- in early mission design (phase A/B) to assess the feasibility and impact of collision avoidance compliance ondesign and operations, and- by spacecraft operators who need more realistic planning tools for operations and manoeuvre planning.
